nary_nodes.label: France heatwave of June 2026
evidence: France has said it recorded an increase of more than 2,000 deaths during the last week of a record-breaking European heatwave in June as forecasters warn of further extreme temperatures on the continent in the next few days.
France saw its hottest day ever on average country-wide on 24 June, with temperatures hitting almost 41C in Paris and half the nation placed under a red heat alert.

Météo-France has issued red alerts for Friday and Saturday for forest fires in the southern part of the country, warning that weather conditions meant the risk of an outbreak was 'very high' compared to summer norms.

nary_nodes.label: European heatwave of June 2026
evidence: France has said it recorded an increase of more than 2,000 deaths during the last week of a record-breaking European heatwave in June as forecasters warn of further extreme temperatures on the continent in the next few days.
News of the death toll comes with parts of Europe, including the UK, braced for more searing temperatures from this weekend.

Climate change is driving up temperatures around the world - but particularly in Europe. It is the fastest warming continent, heating up twice as fast as the global average, according to the Copernicus climate service.

nary_nodes.label: Netherlands heatwave of June 2026
evidence: Unprecedented heat in the Netherlands last week led to about 480 excess deaths, Dutch authorities said on Thursday - most of whom were aged 80 and older.
Temperatures reached almost 40C in parts of the country, with most of the deaths reported in the south and east of the Netherlands where temperatures were highest.

nary_nodes.label: Iberian Peninsula heatwave of July 2026
evidence: In the Iberian Peninsula, Aemet weather service has warned of the possibility of another heatwave.
Portugal's government declared a state of alert which will remain in place until midnight on Tuesday. Temperatures are forecast to exceed 40C in some areas, with overnight temperatures above 25C.
In Spain, areas of the southwest are on orange alert as 40C is expected in some parts.

nary_nodes.label: Southern France wildfires of July 2026
evidence: Météo-France has issued red alerts for Friday and Saturday for forest fires in the southern part of the country, warning that weather conditions meant the risk of an outbreak was 'very high' compared to summer norms.
On Thursday, Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said nearly 7,000 fires had broken out since the start of the summer season, with about 8,700 hectares burned so far.
Nearly 3,000 people were evacuated after a wildfire ignited in the town of Sainte-Marie-la-Mer and spread to Canet-en-Roussillon on Thursday.

nary_nodes.label: Suffolk wildfire of July 2026
evidence: Springwatch presenter Chris Packham calls on politicians to act following a wildfire in Suffolk.
Suffolk County Council says 'declaring a climate emergency does not stop a wildfire from starting'.

nary_nodes.label: French health minister on heatwave deaths
evidence: French health minister Stéphanie Rist adding there had been a 'clear increase' in deaths among those over 45.

nary_nodes.label: French health ministry on underestimation of deaths
evidence: The French health ministry said the figure was likely an 'underestimate' and mortality would 'therefore be higher than these initial figures'.

nary_nodes.label: French interior minister on drowning deaths
evidence: French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez saying on Saturday that 72 people had died by drowning since 18 June.

evidence: The country's health ministry said the number of deaths during a heatwave was 'unprecedented'.
